intro: In this lesson, you will be introduced to your first (of very many) connecting particles in Korean. You can usually use these particles to separate two ideas/phrases/sentences. intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to make comparative and superlative sentences in Korean. Using comparative sentences, you will learn how to make sentences like “I am more beautiful than you” or “he is faster than his brother.” Using superlative sentences, you will learn how to make sentences like “I am the most…

title: Well and Poorly: 잘 and 못
intro: Until now, you have not learned how to say “I am good at something/I do something well” or “I am bad at something/I do something poorly.” In this lesson, you will learn about the words 잘하다 (to do something well) and 못하다 (to do something poorly). 못하다 is very hard to understand perfectly, so I will ease you in by…

title: Asking Questions in Korean: Why, When, Where, Who
intro: In Lesson 7, you learned how irregular words change as a result of adding different additions. This is the first time you have been introduced to adding ~니.

title: Asking Questions in Korean: How, What, Which, How Many
intro: In the previous lesson, you learned about how to make question sentences in Korean. In this lesson, you will build on what you learned in Lesson 21 by learning more ways to ask questions in Korean. Specifically, you will learn how to ask questions using the following words: how, what, which and how many.

title: ㅎ Irregular: Korean Colors, 이렇다, 그렇다 and 저렇다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use colors in Korean by applying the ㅎ irregular. In addition, you will learn about the words 이렇다, 그렇다 and 저렇다 and how the ㅎ irregular can be applied to those words. Let’s get started.

title: Before, After, Since, Within (전/후/이래로/이내)
intro: In Lesson 11, you learned a wide variety of different “time” words that you can use in sentences. In that lesson, I said that there were two more words that were very important when talking about time (전 and 후). In that lesson, I said that I would teach you those two words sometime later. Well, this is now later.

title: Using ~는 것 with 이다
intro: I keep saying this, but you have learned a lot about using the ~는 것 principle. Don’t think that you’re out of the woods yet – because there is still a lot to know. In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~는 것 with 이다. Let’s get started.

title: ~(으)려고, ~(으)러 and ~아/어 보다 (with 적)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about how to use ~려고 and ~러 in sentences to have the meaning of “for the purpose of/in order to.” You will also learn how to add ~어/아 보다 to verbs to have the meaning of “attempt/try to,” which is often used with the noun ‘적’. Let’s get started.

title: Explanations for Difficult Words
intro: This lesson is focused entirely on difficult vocabulary. I will teach you about some words that need to be explained before we can move on to more complex grammar. Specifically, you will learn how to to use: 자기/자신, 훨씬, 관하다/관련하다, 주위, 일단, 전혀/별로, words dealing with weight, and words ending in ~거리다. Let’s get started.

title: Because: ~아/어서

title: Because: ~기 때문에
intro: In the previous lesson, you learned about how to use ~아/어서 to create the meaning of “because” in Korean sentences. There are actually many ways you can create the meaning of ‘because’ in Korean – the most common of those being by connecting two clauses with ~아/어서.

title: The Imperative Mood: ~아/어(요), ~(으)세요, ~아/어라, (으)십시오, ~지 말다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to tell people to do things. If you are a grammar buff, you know this as the Imperative Mood. title: To Give: 주다, ~아/어 주다
intro: In the previous lesson, you learned how to give commands using the imperative voice. In this lesson, you will learn how to use 주다 and how it can be used with the imperative voice. In addition, you will learn how to use ~아/어 주다 when an action is done for you. Let’s get started.

title: Let’s/Shall: ~자, ~ㅂ/읍시다, ~ㄹ/을래(요)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about ~자 and ~ㅂ/읍시다, which are two common endings that you can use to suggest that you do something with another person. In addition, you will learn how to use ~ㄹ/을래(요) which can sometimes be used in similar situations. Let’s get started.

title: One can/cannot – ~ㄹ/을 수 있다/없다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the noun “수” in Korean. With this, you will learn how to say “I can” and “I can’t” with the constructions ~ㄹ/을 수 있다 and ~ㄹ/을 수 없다. Let’s get started.

title: I have to/I need to ~아/어야 하다/되다/지/겠다, ~ㄹ 필요가 있다/없다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~아/어야 하다 to indicate that something must be done. In addition, you will learn about the word 필요하다 and how it can be used to create a similar meaning as ~아/어야 하다. Let’s get started.

intro: In this lesson, you will learn the meanings of ~처럼 and ~듯(이). These are often used to indicate that an action is done “like” something else. We will go over the meanings of both of them, and describe the differences in this lesson. Let’s get started.

title: To include (포함하다), to exclude (제외하다)

title: It doesn’t matter/ Regardless of (상관없다/상관없이)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use the word “상관없다” in sentences, both as a word that can be placed at the end of a sentence (like any other verb/adjective) and as an adverb than can be placed in the middle of a sentence. title: I don’t care: 신경 안 쓰다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use “신경 (안) 쓰다” to say “I care” or “I don’t care.” In order to create this meaning, the process is similar to what you learned in the previous lesson, where you learned how to say “It is irrelevant…” Let’s get started.

title: One should/must not: ~아/어서는 안 되다, ~(으)면 안 되다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about two similar grammatical principles and their (similar) respective meanings. In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~아/어서는 안 되다 to mean “one should not” and ~(으)면 안 되다 to mean “one must not.” We will also look at the positive meaning of using ~(으)면 되다, which is a very natural…

title: Because (of): ~(으)니까 and ~(으)니
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~(으)니까 and ~(으)니 between two clauses to create a meaning that is similar to ~아/어서. Of course, just like every other grammatical principle, there are some subtle nuances that you should know about. Let’s get started.

title: ~구나, ~군 and ~군요
intro: In this lesson you will learn how to add ~구나, ~군 or ~군요 to the end of a sentence. This grammatical form is often said when one realizes a new fact or piece of information. Allow me to break it down more than that. Let’s get started.
sections: Oh! I didn’t realize that…: ~구나, ~군 or ~군요

title: Expressing Surprise or Admiration: ~네(요)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn the meaning of adding “~네(요)” to sentences. This grammatical form has a very similar meaning and usage to ~구나/군/군요, which you learned in the previous lesson. Let’s get started.

title: As soon as (~자마자, ~는 대로, ~자)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the grammatical principle ~자마자 and it’s less common counterpart, ~자. Both have similar meanings, but as always I will dissect each one so you can understand them more clearly by the end of this lesson. Let’s get started.

title: To know, to not know (~ㄹ/을/ㄴ/은 줄 알다/모르다), As you know (~알다시피)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn two grammatical principles that can are commonly used with the verb 알다 (to know). First, you will learn about ~ㄹ/을 줄 알다, and second you will learn about ~다시피. Let’s get started.

title: Negating Nouns and Clauses (아니라, ~는 게 아니라)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use the word 아니라 (from the word 아니다) to negate a preceding noun. In doing so, you will also see how you can negate an entire clause by applying ~는 것 to a verb, adjective or 이다. Let’s get started.
sections: Something is, while something isn’t: 이/가 아니라
A clause is, while another clause isn’t: ~는 게 아니라

title: To decide to do (~기로 하다)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add ~기로 하다 to the end of a sentence or clause to indicate that one “decides to do” an action. The usage and translation are fairly straightforward, to the point that the construction can almost be thought of as an idiom. However, I do feel that this is a grammatical principle…

title: Many meanings of ~다가
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the various usages of ~다가, which is often placed between two clauses. There are many meanings that ~다가 can have, and it is often confused with other grammatical principles that have similar meanings. Because of this confusion, this grammatical principle has plagued learners of…

title: Comparing using fractions and orders of Magnitude
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a variety of new words and grammatical principles that you can use in comparative sentences. Previously, way back in Lesson 19, you learned how to make comparisons in sentences by using ~보다. In this lesson, you will learn how 비교하다 and ~에 비해 can also be used to make comparisons. In…

title: The meaning of ~잖아(요)
intro: In this lesson you will learn how to end sentences with ~잖아 or ~잖아요. Though this is a very common ending in conversational Korean, English speakers often cannot figure out exactly what it means. The main reason for this is simply because it is hard to translate directly into English. In this lesson, there will be…

title: ~거든(요): Because, Other meanings
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add ~거든(요) to the end of a sentence or to connect two clauses. Like many grammatical principles in Korean, the meaning of ~거든 depends on the situation and context of when it is used. In this lesson, I will break down all the possible meanings of ~거든(요) and explain their usages.…

title: ~도록: To an extent, In order to, To make
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the Korean grammatical principle ~도록, which has confused foreign learners of Korean for ages. I think the confusion with this grammatical principal stems from the fact that there are so many translations for the same Korean usage. I will break it all down for you step by step,…

title: ~지 and ~죠
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add ~지 or its formal equivalent ~죠 to the end of a sentence. The meaning that this grammatical form has is usually tricky for foreign learners of Korean to pick up on – but don’t worry, I am here to explain everything to you! Let’s get started!
sections: Turn a Statement into a question using ~지/~죠

title: To end up: ~게 되다
intro: We have discussed the usage of 되다 in many earlier lessons, including Lesson 9, Lesson 14, Lesson 49 and Lesson 80. Using 되다 combined with ~게 (from Lesson 56) will be discussed in this lesson. Let’s get started!

title: 뿐: Just, Only (~ㄹ/을 뿐이다, ~ㄹ/을 뿐만 아니라)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use 뿐 in a variety of situations. First, you will learn how to use 뿐 after a noun. Then, you will learn how to use 뿐 after a verb/adjective – both at the end of a sentence and in the middle of a sentence. Finally, you will learn how to use ~뿐만 아니라 to have the meaning of “not…

Using 뿐 in the middle of a sentence
Not only, but also: ~ㄹ/을 뿐만 아니라

title: If one wants to be able to: ~(으)려면
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to combine two previous grammatical principles to come up with ~(으)려면. Let’s get started.

title: Abbreviated Conjugations: 갖다 and 머물다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the word 갖다, which is an abbreviation of the word 가지다. The Korean language has evolved in such a way that 갖다 can now be thought of as a word, but due to the fact that it is actually an abbreviation, it has atypical grammatical rules. I will break these rules open for you. Let’s…

title: To pretend to: ~은/ㄴ/는 척하다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a 보조동사 that allows you to indicate that one pretends to do something. Let’s get started.

title: Even if: ~더라도
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~더라도 as a connector between two clauses to mean “even if.” Let’s get started!

title: The confusing meanings of ~텐데(요)
intro: Okay, get ready for another lesson filled with grammar explanations. What else would you expect? With this being our 100th lesson, I wanted to make sure it was a good one. Before I say anything else, I want to take just a moment to thank anyone who has actually followed these lessons to this point. It initially…
sections: It is probable that, I suppose that…: ~ㄹ/을 텐데(요)
Using ~ㄹ/을 텐데 (or ~ㄹ/을 테니까) in the middle of a sentence

title: Korean Slang and Abreviations
intro: This lesson will be a bit of a change of pace. After one hundred lessons of HowtoStudyKorean, you probably have a good base of official, written Korean grammar. In this lesson, you will learn some ways that Korean is often changed during speaking. They say that in order to be a musician, you need to study music to…
sections: Abbreviating Particles: 난, 건, 걸, etc…

title: Quoted Abbreviations
intro: In this lesson, you will learn more ways to abbreviate Korean sentences. In the previous lesson, you learned common ways that Korean people shorten their sentences in messaging or when talking on the internet. In this lesson, you will learn how to abbreviate conjugations of quoted sentences. Let’s get started.

title: Lessons 103: 한, 약, ~(으)므로, 전반, 당하다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a variety of smaller grammatical principles that are similar to grammatical principles you have learned previously. title: Adding ~는/은 to More Complicated Things
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the particle ~는/은. Wait a second, didn’t I learn about ~는/은 in Lesson 1? Isn’t that the particle that I have been using in every one of my Korean sentences since I started learning Korean? Isn’t this Lesson 104? Why am I learning about ~는/은 in Lesson 104?

title: Small Grammar Points!
intro: The title of this lesson is: Grammatical principles that I can’t believe I haven’t taught you yet – and I better teach them to you now before we get too deep into more difficult grammatical principles in Unit 5. title: Listing Possibilities/Outcomes: ~든지 (간에)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add ~든지 to the end of a clause. Although this grammatical principle has a fairly straightforward meaning across the board, it can be used in a bunch of different ways. Let’s get started!

title: ~도 Revisited
intro: By now, you have been exposed to the particle ~도 and its function for a while. You are probably quite familiar with how it works, and the meaning it creates when it is added directly to a noun.

title: Past Perfect: ~었~
intro: In this lesson, you will learn the meaning of a grammatical principle that, by this point, you have probably noticed a few times in your Korean studies. Have you ever seen words in the past tense conjugated with an additional ~었~? As in, 했었다 instead of 했다? In this lesson, we will look at the meaning of this…

title: ~나 보다, ~는/ㄴ가 보다
intro: In this lesson, you will how to attach ~ㄴ가/은가/는가/나 보다 to the end of a sentence. That’s a funny looking grammatical principle, isn’t it? Let’s get started.
sections: To guess, think, suppose, to look like: ~는/ㄴ가보다

title: 어쩔 수 없다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use 어쩔 수 없다 and its various forms in sentences. Though not quite a grammatical principle (it’s more of a word combined with ~ㄹ/을 수 없다) its usage is fairly common and quite difficult – enough to warrant me to write a lesson about it. Let’s get started.
sections: There is nothing one can do about something: 어쩔 수 없다

title: ~(이)라도
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add ~(이)라도 to nouns. Though this grammatical principle looks similar to (and sometimes even translates similarly to) ~더라도 (which you learned in Lesson 99), ~(이)라도 is in fact a separate grammatical principle with a separate usage and meaning. Let’s get started.

title: ~는 편이다 – Adding the soft “fairly” to sentences
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use 편, both as a noun and as a grammatical principle to make your sentences softer and more humble. Let’s get started.

title: On one’s way ~는 길
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use 길 as a noun that can replace 것 in the ~는 것 principle. Don’t be confused! This grammatical principle isn’t describing a road… Well, it kind of is. It has a special meaning that we can study as a separate grammatical principle. Let’s get started.
sections: While on my way to/from: ~는 길에
There is no way of/to… ~ㄹ/을 길이 없다

title: ~는 김에
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another noun that is often described by ~는. In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~는 김에. Let’s get started.

title: I Should Have: ~ㄹ/을걸 (그랬다)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about a grammatical principle that looks like it has an entirely different meaning and purpose than it actually does. I remember when I saw ~ㄹ/을걸 for the first time, I said to myself “Oh, I can probably guess what that means!” Boy was I wrong. Let me teach it to you. Let’s get started.
sections: 괜히: Something That You Didn’t Need to Do

title: While in the state of: ~ㄴ/은 채(로)
intro: In this Lesson, you will learn about the special noun, 채. This is another noun that can be used in the ~는 것 principle that takes on a special meaning. In this lesson, you will learn how it can be used. Let’s get started.
sections: While in the state of: ~ㄴ/은 채(로)

title: ~더~ and ~던가
intro: In this lesson, you will be introduced to the grammatical principle ~더~ and the meaning it creates in a sentence. You will apply your knowledge of –더- by combining it with another grammatical principle to create ~던가. Let’s get started.
sections: Asking Questions to Somebody Else Using ~던가

title: Stating a fact from experience: ~더라
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to learn about ~더~ and how it can be combined with ~라. Let’s get started.

title: ~더니 (to notice… then…)

The construction ~더니 is very similar to other clause connectors like ~아/어서, ~(으)니(까) and ~기 때문에, but as always there are some specific…
sections: When the speaker is talking about himself/herself: ~더니
When the speaker is talking about somebody else: ~더니

title: ~다니
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to connect two clauses with ~다니, which will be your first real introduction into the world of compounded quoted grammatical principles. I just made up that term off the top of my head, but let’s get started.

What does this grammatical principle mean?

title: ~다 보면
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to connect two clauses by using the grammatical principle ~다 보면. The grammar within this principle is actually the addition of a few different grammar concepts piled together, but its meaning is simple enough to describe in a short lesson.
sections: If one does something for a while, the next action will occur: ~다 보면

title: ~다 보니(까)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another grammatical principle that requires the use of 보다. Specifically, you will learn how to use ~다(가) 보니까 to connect two clauses. Let’s get started.
sections: While doing something, one realizes: ~다 보니(까)

title: ~아/어 보니(까)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another grammatical principle that contains 보다. In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~아/어 보니까. Let’s get started.
sections: Now that I have done…/Having done… ~아/어 보니(까)

title: To be Worth Doing: ~ㄹ/을 만하다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~ㄹ/을 만하다 to indicate that something is worth doing or possible. In doing so, you will see how these types of sentences can also be expressed using the word 가치. Let’s get started.

title: I said that: ~ㄴ/는다니까
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a Korean grammatical principle that you can use to make your Korean sound extra sassy! You can use this grammatical principle when you are a little bit annoyed at somebody, and what to show your frustration. Let’s get started.

title: To be Grouped or Classified by: ~별
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add ~별 to nouns and the meaning it creates. You will see that it is often attached to nouns to describe another noun, or used with ~로 to act as an adverb. Let’s get started.
sections: To be Grouped or Classified by: ~별(로)

title: To be done in a divisible quantity – ~씩
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to attach ~씩 to indicate that an object, time or action (or something else) will be divided into a specific quantity or regular intervals. Later in the lesson, you will see how ~씩 can be applied to the words 조금 and 가끔. Let’s get started.
sections: To Be Done in a Divisible Quantity: ~씩
Using ~씩 with an Indication of Time

title: Leaving an action in its completed state with 놓다, and an organization of 나다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add ~아/어 놓다 to a verb to indicate that one does an action and the completed state of that action continues. In addition, you will look back at the many ways 나다 can be used and also learn a few more. Let’s get started!
sections: To Complete an Action and Leave it in that State: ~아/어 놓다
Organization and Review of the Many Usages of 나다

title: To cross over, to pass – 넘다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use the word 넘다 to describe that something happens past a particular point or threshold. 넘다 can be used at the end of a sentence, but it is also commonly used in the middle of sentences as 넘게 or 넘어서. Let’s get started.

title: Big Korean Numbers
intro: In Lesson 10, you first learned how to use numbers in Korean. That information was crucial in your ability to count different things in Korean like things, events, minutes, hours, days, months, cars and many other things.

title: The Middle ㅅ: 사이시옷
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about words that contain an extra ㅅ. This is called a 사이시옷, and its inclusion in words is very complex. Luckily, there are a set of rules that I can teach you. Let’s get started!
sections: 사이시옷: Putting ㅅ Within Compound Words

title: ~ㄹ/을수록 – As One Situation Changes, Another Situation Changes
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to attach ~ㄹ/을수록 to the end of a clause. A rather advanced grammatical principle, but something that you should be able to grasp easily. Let’s get started.

title: For there to be no way ~ㄹ/을 리가 없다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn the meaning that is created when 리 is described as a noun. Let’s get started.

title: 성 – Character or a Range of Quality
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the syllable 성. The purpose of this lesson was to discuss the meaning of 성 when used to indicate a range of some quality. sections: 성 (性) = Character or a Range of Some Quality

intro: In this lesson, you will learn about ~기에 and ~길래. These grammatical principles are used to create a meaning of “so” or “because,” which often leads learners of Korean confused with how these may be different than ~아/어서. I will dissect this in this lesson! Let’s get started.

title: ~아/어야: One must do an action in order to do another
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add ~아/어야 to the end of a clause. You saw this grammatical principle in a previous lesson, but only followed by 하다. We will look at how this is used in all other situations. Let’s get started.

title: ~았/었어야 하다 – One Should Have, But Didn’t
intro: In this lesson, we will add complexity to a very common grammatical principle. ~아/어야 하다 was introduced in Lesson 46 as a way to indicate that one must do an action. In the previous lesson, I broke that grammatical principle down by explaining the purpose of ~아/어야 and even indicated that it can be used without the…

title: One Could Have Done, But Did Not
intro: In this lesson, we will add complexity to a very common grammatical principle. ~아/어도 되다 was introduced in Lesson 49 as a way to indicate that one may do an action. title: ~(으)로서 – With a Specific Status
intro: Two similar looking grammatical principles, two completely different meanings. In this lesson and the next one, you will learn how to use ~(으)로서 and ~(으)로써 in Korean sentences. title: ~(으)로써 – From what ingredient, or by what means or tool
intro: In this lesson, we will learn about ~(으)로써, which looks slightly similar to the grammatical principle ~(으)로서 from the previous lesson. Korean people often have trouble remembering which one is which, but let’s make sure that doesn’t happen to you! Let’s get started.
sections: ~(으)로써: From what ingredient, or by what means or tool

title: ~ㄴ/는다니 – Responding in Surprise or Displeasure
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a simple and common way to end your sentences with a bit of attitude. You will learn the subtle meaning of ending your sentences ~ㄴ/는다니, ~다니, ~(이)라니, ~자니, ~(느)냐니 and ~(으)라니. Let’s get started.
sections: Adding this Grammatical Principle to Other Endings

title: ~ㄹ/을걸(요) To state or refute in an unsure way
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to make or refute a statement in doubt by using ~ㄹ/을걸(요). Although typically used in response to what other people say, it can also be used when one is just talking making a guess. title: ~란

title: ~느라고 – A Negative Result Occured Because a Purposeful Action was Done
intro: There are so many ways to create a sentence in Korean where one clause causes the next. Let’s learn about another one! In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~느라고 to connect two clauses to indicate that the reason why the second clause happened is because of the first clause. Of course, it’s not that simple!…

title: ~는 바람에 – A negative result occurred because of an unexpected or unpreventable event
intro: In this lesson, we will learn about ~는 바람에 and touch briefly on the other uses of 바람. This lesson will be similar to the previous lesson because ~는 바람에 and ~느라고 have some similarities, and they both allow a speaker to indicate causality. Let’s get started!
sections: Using 바람 to indicate the clothing one wears
An organization of the uses of 바람

title: ~고는 하다 and ~곤 하다 – One does an action regularly but infrequently
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~고는 하다 (or ~곤 하다). It is a fairly simple grammatical principle to use, and unlike some of the other endings we have learned lately, doesn’t have a lot of subtle nuances to it. Let’s get started!

title: 하필 – Of all possible situations to occur, the most unfortunate one occurs
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the word 하필 and how you can use it in Korean sentences. What does this word mean? What does it translate to? Does it even have a translation? What type of situation should it be used in? We will get to all of this. Let’s get started.

title: 어쩐지 – One doesn’t know the reason and/or only now realizes
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another adverb that is hard to translate to English – 어쩐지. It is commonly used in two types of situations, but are those situations actually different? Or are our English minds deceiving us? Let’s get started.

intro: The purpose of this lesson is to introduce you to trends I have noticed with mimetic words. title: ~(으)려니까 – To intend to do, but

title: ~(으)려다가 – I was going to, but then
intro: In the previous lesson, you saw that you can combine ~(으)려 with ~(으)니까 to combine their meanings. In this lesson, you will continue to expand your understanding of ~려 by connecting it to another grammatical principle.

title: ~(으)려는 Describing an upcoming noun with~려고 하다

title: ~(으)려는 참 and ~(으)려던 참 – One was just about to

title: 경우 – Case or Circumstance

sections: Abbreviation of ~하지 않다: ~지 않다 and ~치 않다

title: ~느냐: Whether or Not
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use a familiar grammatical principle, ~느냐 to create a more complex meaning than what you already have learned. Furthermore, you will learn to add to ~느냐 to make it even more complex. Let’s get started!

title: Describing Upcoming Nouns with ~느냐는
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to describe upcoming nouns with ~느냐, which you learned in the previous lesson. Let’s get started.

title: ~느냐에 따라서 – Depending on…
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to add another layer of complexity to sentences with ~느냐. By using the verb 따르다 in sentences with ~느냐, you can create the meaning of “depending on…” in English. Let’s get started!

title: ~ㄴ/은/는/을/ㄹ 말이다: Stressing or Checking
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how you can end your sentences colloquially with 말. We’ll break down the situations where this would be appropriate and natural. Let’s get started!
sections: ~ㄴ/은/는/을/ㄹ 말이다: Stressing or Checking What was Already Said

title: ~아/어야 말이지 – Expressing Annoyance
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to see how versatile the noun 말 can be. Specifically we will see how using 말 at the end of a sentence, but preceded by something different than the previous lesson, you can create an entirely different meaning. Let’s get started.
sections: ~아/어야 말이지: Expressing Annoyance that Something Must Happen

title: ~(으)니/~기에 말이지 – Emphasizing Fortune or Relief
intro: In this lesson, you will see another way that 말 can be used, this time, by having it follow ~(으)니 or ~기에. We’ll explore the meaning they create. Let’s get started!

title: ~(이)야말로 – Emphasizing Over All Others
intro: In this lesson, we will see the nuanced meaning that ~(이)야말로 can add to a sentence. Let’s get started!
sections: ~(이)야말로: Emphasizing a Noun Over All Others

title: ~ㄹ/을까 말까 – Hesitating or Deciding
intro: In this lesson, you will begin a deep-dive into the verb 말다 to see how it can be used in a variety of situations. Specifically, in this lesson, you will learn how ~ㄹ/을까 말까 is used. Let’s get started!

title: ~거나 말거나: Indifference
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to learn about applications of 말다. Specifically, you will see how it can be used with ~거나. Let’s get started.
sections: ~거나 말거나: Stating Indifference to a Situation

title: ~ㄹ/을락 말락: Stopping or Hesitating
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to learn about applications of 말다. Specifically, you will see how it can be used with ~ㄹ/을락 말락. Let’s get started.

title: ~고 말았다: To End Up Doing
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to learn about 말. In the past few lessons, you have seen how certain grammatical principles are added to some verbs and also attached to 말다. We will steer away from those style of grammatical principles for this lesson, and focus on how 말다 is used with ~고 and ~고야. Let’s get started.
sections: ~고 말겠다: To be sure to do

title: ~다 싶다: Feeling, Thought or Perception
intro: I remember being a few years into my Korean study journey. Two years of being an absolute Korean grammar nerd, I was getting a bit arrogant about how good my understanding of Korean grammar was. It was getting to the point that I was sometimes correcting the grammar of Korean people. Then one day I was reading a…
sections: ~다 싶다: Stating One’s Feeling, Thought or Perception

title: ~(으)면 싶다 – Hope or Wish
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to learn about the uses of 싶다, continuing on from the previous lesson. Specifically, you will learn how to use 싶다 after ~(으)면. Let’s get started.

title: 싶다 – Guess, Assumption and Intention
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to learn about 싶다. In this lesson, you will learn two more uses that follow a similar form after indications of doubt or question. Let’s get started.

title: ~기는(요) – Downplaying Praise or Flattery
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a way to make your responses to praise or flattery more humble sounding. Let’s get started!

title: ~치고 – Without Exception
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to use ~치고 to indicate that there are no exceptions within a group of things. In addition, you will see how adding ~는 to ~치고 changes the nuance slightly. Let’s get started!

title: ~아/어 봤자 – To be Pointless to do
intro: Welcome to Unit 8! I can’t believe that we are 176 lessons in. If you started with me from the beginning and made it this far, you should be really proud of yourself.

title: ~(으)오 and ~(으)오니: Archaic and Formal Connector
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about the structure of a common literary infix: ~오~. That is, a particle that squeezes between words and other grammatical principles. Although this infix is somewhat old-fashioned, it shows up a lot in literature and formal situations. Let’s get started!

title: Using ~구요 Instead of ~고
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a new take on a familiar particle. Specifically, you will see how ~구요 can replace ~고 given the right situation. Let’s get started.

title: ~기 마련이다: Bound to Occur
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about a noun that takes on a complex meaning. Although it’s technically a noun, you can think of it as functioning more like a grammatical principle. In this lesson, you will learn about 마련. Let’s get started.

title: ~ㄴ/은/는/을/ㄹ 듯하다: To seem like
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about a way to express your inferences using a new grammatical principle.This grammatical principle is similar to 것 같다, which you learned in an earlier lesson.. In this lesson, you will learn about 듯하다.

title: ~조차: Even one particular noun
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about ~조차, a particle attached to nouns that has a similar function to ~도. We will explore how ~조차 differs from ~도 and how it adds emphasis. Let’s get started.

title: ~답다: Taking the Qualities of a Noun
intro: In this lesson, you’ll learn how to turn certain nouns into adjectives using ~답다, a pattern that adds the qualities of a noun to a description. Let’s get started.
sections: ~답다: Taking the Qualities of a Noun

title: ~롭다: To Possess a Quality or Characteristic Fully
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another way to turn nouns into adjectives. This time, using the addition ~롭다. Let’s get started!
sections: ~롭다: To possess a quality or characteristic fully

title: ~(이)나마: Accepting an Unsatisfactory Situation
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another particle that can be used to create a meaning similar to ~지만 or ~아/어도. In this lesson, you will learn about ~(이)나마. Let’s get started!

title: ~ㄴ/은/는데다가: Piling on Information
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to combine two grammatical principles that you learned in the past ~ㄴ/은/는데 and ~다가. Let’s get started.

title: ~고서: Sequential or Causal Relationship
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another way to indicate that one action happened after another one in time. We will look at how this is similar to other grammatical principles that have been introduced in previous lessons. Let’s get started.

title: ~고서야: Only After
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another way to indicate that one action happened after another one in time. While this grammatical principle may look similar to what was taught in the previous lesson, it carries a distinct meaning. Let’s get started.

title: ~(으)나: Even Though
intro: In this lesson, and the next few, we will take a deep dive into ~나 and its more complex uses. In this lesson, you will see how ~나 can have a similar meaning to that of ~지만. Let’s get started.

title: ~(으)나: Irrelevance Among Options
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to learn about ~(으)나. In this lesson, you will add to the ways you saw ~(으)나 used by learning about two more meanings for it. Let’s get started!

title: ~(으)나 마나: To be Pointless
intro: In this lesson, you will continue to learn about ~(으)나 by looking at another way that it can be used. In this lesson, you will see it used with 말다 to create 하나 마나. Let’s get started.

title: ~는 둥 마는 둥: Incompletely or Half-heartedly
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another way to use 말다 by applying it to a grammatical principle that allows you to indicate that an action is done halfheartedly or with a lack of focus. Let’s get started.
sections: ~는 둥 마는 둥: Incompletely or Halfheartedly
~-다는/냐는/라는/자는 둥: Going on and on with nonsense

title: ~ㄴ/는단다: A Motherly Contraction of ~ㄴ/는다고 한다
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about a common contraction that creates a motherly tone in Korean. Specifically, you will learn about the contraction of ~ㄴ/는다고 하다. Let’s get started!

title: ~(으)렴 – Gentle Command
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another way to make a command. This way of making commands is much softer and is used by the older generation. In this lesson, you will learn about ~(으)렴. Let’s get started.

title: Naming recurring events, historical events and parts within legal documents (제1회)
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to name recurring events, historical events and parts within legal documents. We’ll explore the counters 회 and 차, and how they work with 제. Let’s get started.
sections: 제(第): Turning One, Two Three into First, Second, Third

title: 그지없다: To not be able to express the extent of an adjective
intro: In this lesson, you will learn how to describe things with adjectives in a more expressive way. This will allow your Korean sentences to carry more emotional weight. Specifically, you’ll learn about the pattern ~기 그지없다. Let’s get started.
sections: 그지없다: To not be able to express the extent of an adjective

title: 겸 and 겸사겸사
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about another pseudo-noun. This one will allow you to express that more than one noun or verb happens simultaneously. In this lesson, you will learn about the noun 겸. Let’s get started.

title: 바 – Referring to a Past Notice and Taking an Opportunity
intro: In this lesson, you will learn about a complex, formal pseudo-noun. This noun is often found in notices and legal documents. In this lesson, you will learn about 바. Let’s get started.
sections: 바: Usage 1: Referring to a Past Notice

title: ~ㄴ/은 셈이다: To be considered as
intro: In this lesson, you will learn another pseudo-noun. This noun allows you to express that certain situations can be considered as something. In this lesson, you will learn about ~ㄴ/은 셈이다. Let’s get started.

title: ~은/는커녕: Far From
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a particle with a lot of meaning packed into it. In this lesson, you will learn about ~은/는커녕, which is used to stress a situation to the extreme. Let’s get started.

title: 부리다: To Display a Behavior or Attitude
intro: Lesson 200! I’m so proud of what we have accomplished. We started writing Korean lessons in 2011 and this lesson is being uploaded in 2025. It took us 14 years, but we managed to finally get to 200. I wrote a similar message to this at 100. When I wrote Lesson 100, I had no children. Now, at Lesson 200, I have 7-…
sections: 부리다: To Display a Behavior or Attitude

title: ~(으)리라고: To Think Something Will Happen
intro: Unit 9! I can’t believe it! 201 lessons in! If you’ve made it this far, you are probably speaking Korean really well. From this point on, our grammar lessons will likely get you from being 98% Korean sounding to 99% Korean sounding. Hold on tight!

title: ~(으)려니: A Settled Assumption
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a grammatical construction used to express an assumption or expectation that a speaker has settled on in their own mind. Depending on the context, it can also convey a sense of resignation or acceptance. In this lesson, you will learn about ~(으)려니. Let’s get started.

title: ~거니: A Confident Assumption
intro: In this lesson, you will learn a way to express your opinion on something that you have largely settled on as true. This grammatical principle is commonly used to describe what one figured must be the case, even though the fact has not yet been confirmed. In this lesson, you will learn about ~거니. Let’s get started.
